title: Radiotherapy ± Chemotherapy in Older Adults with Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study
summary:
Head and neck cancers are the sixth most common cancer worldwide and cause around 450,000 deaths every year. In Germany, about a third of all patients are now 70 years or older at the time of diagnosis, and this proportion has been steadily growing for years. Despite this trend, there is little scientific evidence on how best to treat this vulnerable patient group. Some major clinical trials have even excluded older patients, so it remains relatively unclear how effective or burdensome combined chemoradiotherapy actually is in older age. At the same time, everyday clinical experience shows that treatment decisions for older patients vary widely, because frailty, comorbidities, and functional limitations are more common than in younger patients. In addition, treatment goals sometimes differ between younger and older patients, something that previous studies have not adequately addressed.

The planned SENIOR-2 study aims to close these knowledge gaps. In a nationwide prospective cohort study across Germany, around 1,000 patients aged 70 or older who are receiving radiotherapy for a locally advanced head and neck tumor will be followed. The study will capture the entire course of treatment along with all relevant medical, functional, and psychosocial parameters. This includes treatment details such as radiation dose, the type and dosing of concurrent chemotherapy, deviations from the treatment plan, and reasons for treatment discontinuation. Acute and chronic side effects will also be systematically documented, as will changes in quality of life, measured using validated questionnaires.

A particular focus is on the actual benefit of concurrent chemotherapy in older patients. Since many of these patients cannot receive cisplatin, the most commonly used chemotherapy drug, alternative treatment regimens and their effectiveness will also be examined. The study will further investigate whether geriatric screening can help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from concurrent chemotherapy. In addition, the researchers will analyze whether and to what extent treatment leads to long-term limitations, such as permanent dependence on a feeding tube. Patients' personal treatment goals will also be recorded at the start of treatment.

Beyond medical and psychosocial aspects, the study also addresses health economic questions, including treatment costs, length of hospital stays, and the financial burden patients report over the course of treatment. The resulting comprehensive dataset is intended to help bring more structure to the currently highly variable treatment of older patients with head and neck cancer, enable individualized treatment recommendations, and ultimately lay the groundwork for future randomized trials. Overall, the project aims to improve care for older patients in Germany and worldwide, and to align treatment decisions more closely with their individual needs.
conditions: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx

interventions.name: Patients with HNSCC will be asked to complete questionnaires regarding their quality of life (EQ-5D-5L, EORTC QLQ-C30, and QLQ-HN43), as well as their treatment goals and regrets about their treatment decisions. Questionnaires will be conducted at up to 7 time points during the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
	HNSCC of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx
	Formal indication for concurrent chemoradiotherapy:
Primary (chemo)radiotherapy: histologically confirmed locally (cT3 or cT4) and/or regionally (cN1-3) advanced HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx), according to the 9th UICC TNM classification
or
Adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy: resected HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx) with at least one of these histopathological high-risk characteristics:
	Positive resection margin (defined here as ≤ 1 mm distance between the tumor and the resection margin), as defined in the postoperative pathology report and/or
	Extranodal extension, as defined in the postoperative pathology report
	Written consent to participate in the stud
Exclusion criteria:
	Planned for palliative radiotherapy (i.e., prescribed total dose in EQD2 (α/β=10 Gy) < 55 Gy)
	Cancer arising outside of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx (e.g., nasopharynx carcinoma, sinonasal cancer, other paranasal sinus tumors, or head and neck cancer of unknown primary).
	Any previous radiation therapy in the head and neck region (oral cavity, nose/oropharynx/hypopharynx, larynx, salivary gland, nasal cavity/sinuses, thyroid gland, cervical esophagus, skin tumors in the facial region)
	Additional invasive malignancy within the last 3 years prior to planned study inclusion
o	Participants with adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or carcinoma in situ (e.g., cervical carcinoma in situ or breast carcinoma in situ) are not excluded.
	Unequivocal distant metastatic disease at the time of planned study inclusion
	Patients under legal supervision or guardianship
	Patients who are dependent on the investigator or the medical staff of the study team 
	Suspected lack of compliance
	Insufficient knowledge of German language
